title: How an OpenAI influencer trip backfired
excerpt: A brand trip hosted by OpenAI plopped influencers into a nature-filled, picturesque weekend getaway. The trip has triggered backlash from audiences.
content_html:
The brand trip is a right of passage for influencers. It’s a mark of legitimacy that a sponsor wants to invite them on an all-expenses-paid vacation, often with luxurious freebies and activities. Trips can also spur hard feelings from uninvited influencers, trigger criticism from the public, and project a certain frivolousness.

Usually it is fast fashion companies or beauty brands flying out influencers with the goal of flooding social media with sponsored content. This time, it was a major AI company.

Over the weekend, several influencers began posting about OpenAI’s “first ever brand trip,” which appears to have taken place outside of New York City at a nature-filled retreat (for those curious, it looks to be the Instagram-bait Wildflower Farms). The trip was marketed as “Summer Club,” and influencers posted photos and videos from their cabins, showing off branded merch and monogrammed pajamas and talking vaguely about the scheduled programming. Many of the content creators appear to be in the career and business niches, posting about workplace culture or about being CEOs. Grace McCarrick, who has 145,000 followers on TikTok, vlogged from her suite as she ran a bath at night. Another influencer, Nat Lucy (57,000 followers), filmed herself spotting a deer outside of her cabin. All hell broke loose.

“People will literally sell their soul and their planet down the river for a nice free hotel room,” one commenter on TikTok wrote under McCarrick’s video. “Wow! Beautiful greenery! They should put a data center there!” reads a comment on Lucy’s post. Most of the videos got relatively little traction: McCarrick’s video has just under 300 likes, and Lucy’s video has fewer than 15,000 views. It’s measly engagement compared to what other splashy brand trips can command — but videos reacting to the trip have made it something of a scandal (a pair of clips alone has over half a million combined views).

Many of the comments on the influencers’ videos cite the environmental effects of the AI boom, the contentious buildout of data centers across the US, and the potential for job replacement or job loss as a result of companies integrating AI in the workplace. Some also questioned why so many of the content creators who went on the trip appeared to be young women, as if OpenAI was targeting a specific demographic via media they were more connected to (though based on photos and videos posted to social media, there were men on the trip, too). According to Pew, even as the AI usage gap between men and women has all but disappeared, women tend to view AI more negatively and are twice as likely to say AI will negatively impact them personally. Some audiences wondered whether female influencers were essentially being used to launder the reputation of an industry under scrutiny.

McCarrick, who describes herself as a creator who talks about “soft skills we need at work to millions online and to teams like Spotify, Amazon, Uber and DoorDash,” has since made multiple videos responding to commenters accusing her of essentially abandoning her morals for a fancy trip. On LinkedIn she wrote that she “genuinely had no idea that people were this anti-AI,” and that the negative response to her videos exposed her to “the shocking AI psychosis running rampant online” — by which she means anger about AI, not the more common definition of being driven to paranoia or delusions of grandeur by using AI. People in the real world “do not run around like a chicken with their heads cut off, screaming about water usage and wildlife and (curiously) fascism,” she wrote.

None of the influencers The Verge reached out to responded to requests for comment. OpenAI said creator marketing is part of how they reach people and that the event was meant to be educational.

“Creators are an important part of our community and how people get information and learn about our products today,” OpenAI spokesperson Edie Campbell-Urban said in an email. “We welcome healthy debate as AI becomes more prevalent, and we value creators who choose to engage with us, attend our events, ask tough questions, and learn alongside everyone else. We’ll continue to value them, just as we do traditional media and other marketing partners.”

Setting aside the backlash to the trip for a moment, a few things stand out. First, all things considered, this appears to be a relatively simple trip. That’s not to say it wasn’t luxurious — the rooms at the retreat cost upwards of $2,000 a night — but it is nothing compared to the brands that go all out in order to milk content from every last moment (some commenters poked fun at the fact that it was a domestic trip, not a far-flung, international vacation). Second, there’s a sense that everyone involved is testing the waters: Multiple influencers noted it was the first brand trip they’d attended, and one influencer indicated they were not paid for their attendance, which big brands often do for top talent. Third and most interestingly, the goals of the trip are muddled: It’s not entirely clear what the influencers were actually doing on the trip, because there is surprisingly little content online from the event. Typically, if an influencer is on a brand trip it’s inescapable — every little luxury, every meal, every activity is TikToked and photo dumped. Instead of content about the capabilities of ChatGPT, the videos and photos are largely aspirational lifestyle content focused on the free swag and pretty setting — and even then, there’s a conspicuous lack of content, period. There isn’t the same flood of picturesque montages, clips from expert sessions or Q&As, or summaries of what a creator learned from their time with OpenAI. At least not yet.

AI companies have used influencer marketing in straightforward ways, like paying creators to make content about their product offerings. But they’ve also dabbled in the kind of influencer marketing people expert from more traditional consumer brands: Anthropic has hosted more lowkey influencer dinners at trendy locations with lifestyle influencers, and there are rumblings of a second OpenAI trip on the West Coast.

As backlash to the industry has grown, AI companies have adjusted how they communicate with the public: “Your jobs will soon be obsolete” has clearly not been the right framing for why people should trust these companies or get on board with their mission. Instead, AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to add a bit of human touch, whether that’s through in-person pop-up coffee shops, stylized merch drops, or ad campaigns that take concerns people have about AI and try to turn them into pro-AI inspirational content.

What better way to reach consumers directly than through the talking heads they already know and trust? Influencers are a convenient vessel, both for brands looking to disseminate their message and for the inevitable backlash from audiences who give them a platform in the first place. In this case, the content broke containment out of the girlboss-style business circles into the mainstream — an AI brand trip dressed up as an aspirational lifestyle retreat is both confusing and enraging to a public fatigued by this line of work. By tapping a certain kind of creator for a weekend of sponsored content, OpenAI is able to test a new audience without fully committing; it’s the content creators, after all, who will get the angry comments, whose faces will be plastered on the backgrounds of an ever-increasing number of reaction videos (influencers received similar backlash for a Shein brand trip in 2023). The AI industry wants the soft power and cultural relevance influencers wield and realized the price of reaching their audience is surprisingly cheap. You get what you pay for.

sentences.en: First, all things considered, this appears to be a relatively simple trip.
sentences.zh: 首先，综合考虑，这似乎是一次相对简单的旅行。

sentences.en: That’s not to say it wasn’t luxurious — the rooms at the retreat cost upwards of $2,000 a night — but it is nothing compared to the brands that go all out in order to milk content from every last moment (some commenters poked fun at the fact that it was a domestic trip, not a far-flung, international vacation).
sentences.zh: 这并不是说它不豪华——度假村的房间每晚价格高达 2,000 美元——但与那些竭尽全力从最后一刻榨取营养的品牌相比，这根本算不了什么（一些评论者嘲笑这是一次国内旅行，而不是一次遥远的国际度假）。

sentences.en: Second, there’s a sense that everyone involved is testing the waters: Multiple influencers noted it was the first brand trip they’d attended, and one influencer indicated they were not paid for their attendance, which big brands often do for top talent.
sentences.zh: 其次，有一种感觉，每个参与其中的人都在试水：多名有影响力的人指出，这是他们参加的第一次品牌之旅，一位有影响力的人表示，他们没有因为参加而获得报酬，而大品牌经常为顶尖人才这样做。

sentences.en: Third and most interestingly, the goals of the trip are muddled: It’s not entirely clear what the influencers were actually doing on the trip, because there is surprisingly little content online from the event.
sentences.zh: 第三，也是最有趣的是，这次旅行的目标很混乱：并不完全清楚这些有影响力的人在这次旅行中实际上做了什么，因为网上关于这次活动的内容出人意料地少。

sentences.en: Typically, if an influencer is on a brand trip it’s inescapable — every little luxury, every meal, every activity is TikToked and photo dumped.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，如果一个有影响力的人正在进行品牌之旅，这是不可避免的——每一件小奢侈、每顿饭、每一项活动都会被抖音和照片抛弃。

sentences.en: Instead of content about the capabilities of ChatGPT, the videos and photos are largely aspirational lifestyle content focused on the free swag and pretty setting — and even then, there’s a conspicuous lack of content, period.
sentences.zh: 这些视频和照片不是有关 ChatGPT 功能的内容，而是主要是理想的生活方式内容，专注于免费赠品和漂亮的环境 - 即便如此，内容也明显缺乏。

sentences.en: There isn’t the same flood of picturesque montages, clips from expert sessions or Q&As, or summaries of what a creator learned from their time with OpenAI.
sentences.zh: 没有同样大量的风景如画的蒙太奇、专家会议或问答的剪辑，也没有创作者从 OpenAI 中学到的东西的总结。

sentences.en: At least not yet.
sentences.zh: 至少现在还没有。

blocks.html_en: AI companies have used influencer marketing in straightforward ways, like paying creators to make content about their product offerings. But they’ve also dabbled in the kind of influencer marketing people expert from more traditional consumer brands: Anthropic has hosted more lowkey influencer dinners at trendy locations with lifestyle influencers, and there are rumblings of a second OpenAI trip on the West Coast.

sentences.en: AI companies have used influencer marketing in straightforward ways, like paying creators to make content about their product offerings.
sentences.zh: 人工智能公司以简单的方式使用影响力营销，例如付费创作者制作有关其产品的内容。

sentences.en: But they’ve also dabbled in the kind of influencer marketing people expert from more traditional consumer brands: Anthropic has hosted more lowkey influencer dinners at trendy locations with lifestyle influencers, and there are rumblings of a second OpenAI trip on the West Coast.
sentences.zh: 但他们也涉足了来自更传统消费品牌的影响者营销专家：Anthropic 在时尚地点与生活方式影响者举办了更为低调的影响者晚宴，并且有传言称 OpenAI 将在西海岸进行第二次旅行。

blocks.html_en: As backlash to the industry has grown, AI companies have adjusted how they communicate with the public: “Your jobs will soon be obsolete” has clearly not been the right framing for why people should trust these companies or get on board with their mission. Instead, AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to add a bit of human touch, whether that’s through in-person pop-up coffee shops, stylized merch drops, or ad campaigns that take concerns people have about AI and try to turn them into pro-AI inspirational content.

sentences.en: As backlash to the industry has grown, AI companies have adjusted how they communicate with the public: “Your jobs will soon be obsolete” has clearly not been the right framing for why people should trust these companies or get on board with their mission.
sentences.zh: 随着对该行业的强烈反对，人工智能公司调整了与公众沟通的方式：“你的工作很快就会过时”显然不是人们应该信任这些公司或参与他们的使命的正确框架。

sentences.en: Instead, AI companies like OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to add a bit of human touch, whether that’s through in-person pop-up coffee shops, stylized merch drops, or ad campaigns that take concerns people have about AI and try to turn them into pro-AI inspirational content.
sentences.zh: 相反，像 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 这样的人工智能公司试图增加一点人情味，无论是通过面对面的快闪咖啡店、风格化的商品投放，还是通过广告活动来消除人们对人工智能的担忧，并试图将其转化为支持人工智能的励志内容。

blocks.html_en: What better way to reach consumers directly than through the talking heads they already know and trust? Influencers are a convenient vessel, both for brands looking to disseminate their message and for the inevitable backlash from audiences who give them a platform in the first place. In this case, the content broke containment out of the girlboss-style business circles into the mainstream — an AI brand trip dressed up as an aspirational lifestyle retreat is both confusing and enraging to a public fatigued by this line of work. By tapping a certain kind of creator for a weekend of sponsored content, OpenAI is able to test a new audience without fully committing; it’s the content creators, after all, who will get the angry comments, whose faces will be plastered on the backgrounds of an ever-increasing number of reaction videos (influencers received similar backlash for a Shein brand trip in 2023). The AI industry wants the soft power and cultural relevance influencers wield and realized the price of reaching their audience is surprisingly cheap. You get what you pay for.

sentences.en: What better way to reach consumers directly than through the talking heads they already know and trust?
sentences.zh: 还有什么比通过他们已经认识并信任的代言人来直接接触消费者更好的方式呢？

sentences.en: Influencers are a convenient vessel, both for brands looking to disseminate their message and for the inevitable backlash from audiences who give them a platform in the first place.
sentences.zh: 有影响力的人是一个方便的载体，无论是对于希望传播其信息的品牌来说，还是对于首先为他们提供平台的受众来说不可避免的强烈反对。

sentences.en: In this case, the content broke containment out of the girlboss-style business circles into the mainstream — an AI brand trip dressed up as an aspirational lifestyle retreat is both confusing and enraging to a public fatigued by this line of work.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，内容打破了女老板式商业圈的束缚，进入了主流——一场人工智能品牌之旅被打扮成一种理想的生活方式隐居，这对于厌倦了这一行的公众来说既令人困惑又愤怒。

sentences.en: By tapping a certain kind of creator for a weekend of sponsored content, OpenAI is able to test a new audience without fully committing; it’s the content creators, after all, who will get the angry comments, whose faces will be plastered on the backgrounds of an ever-increasing number of reaction videos (influencers received similar backlash for a Shein brand trip in 2023).
sentences.zh: 通过利用特定类型的创作者在周末提供赞助内容，OpenAI 能够在不完全投入的情况下测试新受众；毕竟，受到愤怒评论的将是内容创作者，他们的脸将出现在越来越多的反应视频的背景中（影响者在 2023 年 Shein 品牌之旅中也受到了类似的强烈反对）。

sentences.en: The AI industry wants the soft power and cultural relevance influencers wield and realized the price of reaching their audience is surprisingly cheap.
sentences.zh: 人工智能行业希望影响者拥有软实力和文化相关性，并意识到接触受众的成本出奇的便宜。

sentences.en: You get what you pay for.
sentences.zh: 一分钱一分货。

blocks.html_en: • Mia Sato

sentences.en: Mia Sato
sentences.zh: 佐藤米亚

content_html_zh:
品牌之旅是影响者的通行权。 赞助商希望邀请他们参加全费用带薪假期，通常还提供豪华的免费赠品和活动，这是合法性的标志。 旅行也会激起不请自来的影响者的不满，引发公众的批评，并表现出某种轻浮的态度。

通常是快时尚公司或美容品牌派出有影响力的人，目的是让社交媒体充斥赞助内容。 这一次，是一家大型人工智能公司。

周末，几位有影响力的人开始发布有关 OpenAI 的“第一次品牌之旅”的信息，这次旅行似乎是在纽约市郊外一个充满自然风光的度假胜地进行的（对于那些好奇的人来说，它看起来是 Instagram 上的野花农场）。 这次旅行被宣传为“夏季俱乐部”，有影响力的人发布了他们小屋的照片和视频，展示了品牌商品和印有字母组合的睡衣，并含糊地谈论了预定的节目。 许多内容创作者似乎都处于职业和商业领域，发布有关职场文化或首席执行官的内容。 格蕾丝·麦卡里克 (Grace McCarrick) 在 TikTok 上拥有 145,000 名粉丝，她晚上在套房里一边洗澡一边发布视频博客。 另一位影响者 Nat Lucy（57,000 名粉丝）拍摄了自己在小屋外发现一只鹿的视频。 一切都崩溃了。

“人们实际上会为了一间漂亮的免费酒店房间而出卖自己的灵魂和地球，”TikTok 上的一位评论者在麦卡里克的视频下写道。 “哇！ 美丽的绿化！ 他们应该在那里建立一个数据中心！” 阅读对露西帖子的评论。 大多数视频的吸引力相对较小：McCarrick 的视频只有不到 300 个点赞，而 Lucy 的视频只有不到 15,000 次观看。 与其他引人注目的品牌旅行相比，这种参与度微乎其微，但对这次旅行的反应视频却让它成为了一场丑闻（仅两个视频的综合观看次数就超过了 50 万）。

对影响者视频的许多评论都提到了人工智能热潮对环境的影响、美国各地有争议的数据中心建设，以及公司将人工智能融入工作场所可能导致的工作替代或失业。 一些人还质疑为什么参加这次旅行的内容创作者中有这么多是年轻女性，就好像 OpenAI 通过与她们联系更紧密的媒体针对特定人群（尽管根据社交媒体上发布的照片​​和视频，这次旅行中也有男性）。 皮尤研究中心的数据显示，尽管男性和女性之间的人工智能使用差距几乎消失，但女性往往对人工智能持更负面的看法，并且认为人工智能会对她们个人产生负面影响的可能性是女性的两倍。 一些观众想知道女性影响者是否本质上被用来洗白一个受到审查的行业的声誉。

麦卡里克将自己描述为一位创作者，向数以百万计的在线用户以及 Spotify、亚马逊、Uber 和 DoorDash 等团队谈论“我们工作中需要的软技能”。此后，麦卡里克制作了多个视频来回应评论者，这些评论者指责她为了一次奇特的旅行而实质上放弃了自己的道德。 她在 LinkedIn 上写道，她“真的不知道人们如此反人工智能”，对她视频的负面反应让她接触到了“网上猖獗的令人震惊的人工智能精神病”——她指的是对人工智能的愤怒，而不是更常见的定义，即因使用人工智能而陷入偏执或妄想。 她写道，现实世界中的人们“不会像一只被砍掉头的鸡一样到处乱跑，尖叫着用水、野生动物和（奇怪的）法西斯主义”。

The Verge 的影响者均未回应置评请求。 OpenAI 表示，创作者营销是他们接触人们的方式的一部分，该活动旨在具有教育意义。

OpenAI 发言人 Edie Campbell-Urban 在一封电子邮件中表示：“创作者是我们社区的重要组成部分，也是人们获取信息和了解我们产品的方式。” “随着人工智能变得越来越普遍，我们欢迎健康的辩论，我们重视那些选择与我们互动、参加我们的活动、提出棘手问题并与其他人一起学习的创造者。 我们将继续重视他们，就像我们重视传统媒体和其他营销合作伙伴一样。”

暂时抛开对这次旅行的强烈反对，有几件事很引人注目。 首先，综合考虑，这似乎是一次相对简单的旅行。 这并不是说它不豪华——度假村的房间每晚价格高达 2,000 美元——但与那些竭尽全力从最后一刻榨取营养的品牌相比，这根本算不了什么（一些评论者嘲笑这是一次国内旅行，而不是一次遥远的国际度假）。 其次，有一种感觉，每个参与其中的人都在试水：多名有影响力的人指出，这是他们参加的第一次品牌之旅，一位有影响力的人表示，他们没有因为参加而获得报酬，而大品牌经常为顶尖人才这样做。 第三，也是最有趣的是，这次旅行的目标很混乱：并不完全清楚这些有影响力的人在这次旅行中实际上做了什么，因为网上关于这次活动的内容出人意料地少。 通常情况下，如果一个有影响力的人正在进行品牌之旅，这是不可避免的——每一件小奢侈、每顿饭、每一项活动都会被抖音和照片抛弃。 这些视频和照片不是有关 ChatGPT 功能的内容，而是主要是理想的生活方式内容，专注于免费赠品和漂亮的环境 - 即便如此，内容也明显缺乏。 没有同样大量的风景如画的蒙太奇、专家会议或问答的剪辑，也没有创作者从 OpenAI 中学到的东西的总结。 至少现在还没有。

人工智能公司以简单的方式使用影响力营销，例如付费创作者制作有关其产品的内容。 但他们也涉足了来自更传统消费品牌的影响者营销专家：Anthropic 在时尚地点与生活方式影响者举办了更为低调的影响者晚宴，并且有传言称 OpenAI 将在西海岸进行第二次旅行。

随着对该行业的强烈反对，人工智能公司调整了与公众沟通的方式：“你的工作很快就会过时”显然不是人们应该信任这些公司或参与他们的使命的正确框架。 相反，像 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 这样的人工智能公司试图增加一点人情味，无论是通过面对面的快闪咖啡店、风格化的商品投放，还是通过广告活动来消除人们对人工智能的担忧，并试图将其转化为支持人工智能的励志内容。

还有什么比通过他们已经认识并信任的代言人来直接接触消费者更好的方式呢？ 有影响力的人是一个方便的载体，无论是对于希望传播其信息的品牌来说，还是对于首先为他们提供平台的受众来说不可避免的强烈反对。 在这种情况下，内容打破了女老板式商业圈的束缚，进入了主流——一场人工智能品牌之旅被打扮成一种理想的生活方式隐居，这对于厌倦了这一行的公众来说既令人困惑又愤怒。 通过利用特定类型的创作者在周末提供赞助内容，OpenAI 能够在不完全投入的情况下测试新受众；毕竟，受到愤怒评论的将是内容创作者，他们的脸将出现在越来越多的反应视频的背景中（影响者在 2023 年 Shein 品牌之旅中也受到了类似的强烈反对）。 人工智能行业希望影响者拥有软实力和文化相关性，并意识到接触受众的成本出奇的便宜。 一分钱一分货。
